script: Everyone assumed I'd always drive—until I finally said no and they gas‑pedaled.. I am the only one in my squad who owns a car, so I'd drive a few times, no biggie. But soon it flipped from a favor to a job. Every time we planned a hang, people would text, "What time you picking us up?" instead of, "Can you drive?" And gas? Nobody ever chipped in. Parking fees? I'd pay. (I know, right?) One weekend I said, "Let's meet at the restaurant instead; got errands first." One friend shot back, "That makes things harder for everyone else." I replied, "Exactly. That's why I am always driving." The room went quiet. (Literally insane.) After that, I stopped offering to drive unless someone asked. If it was a longer trip, I'd say, "Let's split gas." Most people were like, "Cool, no problem." The only one who didn't? That same friend who never offered a dime for fuel. Apparently, because I have a car, saving everyone else money is my responsibility. (Honestly, the audacity.)
